x: As regards Alec Olney's record breaking run on the first leg, this was simply superlative running, and when you think back on some of the well-known runners who have done this stage and yet not come within a minute of Olney's time, well all we can say is that Vern Blowfield was not disgraced in hand…
At the bell he was on the shoulder of Theys, the Belgian, but when the latter made his effort, Bill was forced to drop back and Olney then came by him to gain second place.

Pirie, both just out of the junior stage, and he beat such men as Burfitt, Olney and Jimmy Wood. We also had Chas Walker and Ray Tooby qualifying for the final of this event and this speaks well for our strength at this distance.
John Bromley went off with the lead over the long 7th stage, but with Pirie and Olney running stride for stride, they soon overhauled him and went well away into the lead.

S.L.H. had given it to Peter Driver another of their young but very talented members and he set up for them what proved to be an unassailable lead with a time of 28.52 which beat by 17 seconds the October effort of Pirie and Olney which it will be remembered was considered to be an almost fantastic effort.

Barratt of Ealing was an easy winner in 43.17, followed by Olney 44.13, and Ingles another minute back, third Peter Bagnall ran well to be 4th in 45.42, but he had no backing from the rest who included Short 9th, Gebbett 12th, Abbott 13th, L.

Len Marchant had to be content with fifth place in a fast-run 880 yards and George Lucas ran well to gain third place behind Lataster (Holland) and Olney (TVH) in the 3 miles, Len Herbert coming through late to finish sixth."
